name: DFW pre-1950 pier and beam
description: Frame bungalow or Minimal Traditional cottage on pier and beam, wood lap, brick or stone cladding, built before 1950 with no insulation (most attics since topped up), single-pane wood or steel windows and floor-furnace or wall-heater heat; any ducts are a later addition. Every value is an estimate to seed the questionnaire; inspect and override.

era.code_basis: No statewide energy code in Texas before September 2001 (SECO); builder practice only.

style.typical_cladding: wood lap siding, brick or stone veneer

sources.citation: RhoeFlow DFW era template research (claude/01-plan/dfw-era-template-research.md), section Era by era: Before 1950. Every value, its range, evidence type and confidence.
Huang, Hanford and Yang, LBNL-44636 (1999): West South Central prototype houses, pre-1950 no insulation, 1950-79 R-7 ceiling and uninsulated walls, 1980s R-27 roof and R-11 walls

Chan, Joh and Sherman, Analysis of air leakage measurements of US houses (LBNL, Energy and Buildings 2013): leakage by year built (pre-1960 2.2x post-2000, 1960s 1.9x, 1970s 1.8x, 1980s 1.5x, 1990s 1.15x), vented crawlspace about 24% above slab; NL 0.55 is about 10 ACH50
NREL ResStock housing characteristics (develop branch): Texas and climate zone 3A insulation, window, foundation and infiltration distributions by vintage; duct leakage and insulation are assumptions

IECC 2015 Tables R303.1.3(1) and R303.1.3(3), default U-factor and SHGC for unlabeled windows: metal single 1.20, metal double 0.80, nonmetal single 0.95; SHGC single clear 0.8, double clear 0.7 (Seattle adoption text)
Cummings et al., FSEC 1990: central Florida homes over 20 years old averaged about 17 ACH50, homes under 10 years about 8; return leaks about 10% of air handler flow
Green Building Advisor on Austin Energy audits (2009): 310 homes 10+ years old averaged 22% duct leakage
DFW foundation practice: pier and beam common through the 1950s into the 1960s, slab after; post-tensioned slabs from about 1976 (Dallas Morning News marketplace, sponsored content)
Eric Love, Truficient field data from 1,000+ DFW installs, as recorded in RhoeFlow plan v2 §Manual J (claude/01-plan/research-and-plan.md)

ceiling_insulation_cavity_r.basis: R-7: the poor quarter of Texas pre-1950 homes as they stand today (ResStock: 18% uninsulated, 16% R-7, the rest R-13 or more). As built there was none (LBNL prototype), and the range keeps that. Measure the depth in the attic and override.

wall_insulation_cavity_r.basis: Uninsulated frame walls were standard (LBNL prototype; ResStock shows all Texas homes of this age without wall insulation). An asserted default of uninsulated, not an unknown. Confirm at an outlet box or the attic top plate; R-11 if batts are present.

window_ufactor.basis: Single-pane wood or steel sash: code default U 0.95 for an unlabeled single-pane wood window (steel runs about 1.2 to 1.3). Override if the windows have been replaced.

window_shgc.basis: Code default SHGC for single clear glass. Interior shading is entered separately.

air_leakage.basis: Estimate: about 2.2 times a post-2000 house and 24% more for a vented crawlspace (Chan 2013); ResStock median 20 for climate zone 3A; Florida homes this old measured about 17 (Cummings 1990). A blower-door result replaces this.

duct_insulation_r.basis: R-4: old metal duct with wrap or early flex (ResStock assumes R-4 before 2000; an assumption, no measurements found). Read the flex jacket label if visible.

duct_leakage_to_outside.basis: 20% of fan flow to outside, the most common ResStock class; Austin audits of older homes averaged 22% total. Low confidence. A duct-blaster result replaces this.

sanity_band.basis: Unimproved pre-1980 DFW homes run roughly 350 to 450 ft2 per ton in Texas heat (plan §Manual J). The same band for every pre-1980 template until the owner sets one per era in the template editor (WO-03 D9).
